To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) weathered roof cement is not a safe source of asbestos exposure, (2) weathered roof products should be treated as a hazardous substance, and (3) workers should be protected from exposure to asbestos by the use of personal protection equipment and by the use of engineering controls.

(1) asbestos-containing roof cement is friable and releases uncoated chrysotile fibers during weathering and handling, (2) these fibers can be inhaled and deposited in the lungs, and (3) the presence of uncoated chrysolite fibers in the lungs can lead to mesothelioma.

(1) the presence of chrysotile asbestos in roof cement is not “encapsulated”; (2) chrysotile fibers are released from weathered roof cements; (3) the released fibers are not coated with asphalt; and (4) the released fibers may pose an inhalation exposure risk to workers who remove weathering roof cement.
